request: I want the bloomery check command to have progress updates while running on a user terminal (we shouldn't emit events in CI like environments).  I'd like to see how many derivations have been built/need to be built/are pulled from a cache/total metrics, and a counter showing how many of the overall checks are complete.  We should only emit terminal event updates when one of the metrics changes.

reviewResults.summary: The implementation has reproducible gaps in metric accuracy and timeliness: unsupported Nix activity can become known zero work, per-derivation successes are not reflected until a whole Nix request exits, and some final check outcomes are published only after all workers finish. The initial snapshot and terminal-width handling also miss the specified rendering behavior; piped-log write errors are swallowed.

findings.title: Unrecognized Nix activity is reported as known zero work
findings.evidence: `saw_activity` is set only for recognized build starts or substitutions successfully mapped through output metadata. Unrecognized records and substitutions without metadata leave it false; `finish` then emits `DerivationMetadataAvailable`, which makes the reducer display zero for every derivation metric. The test `malformed_and_unknown_records_do_not_change_collected_metrics` also expects that event after malformed/unknown records, despite the design requiring unavailable metrics to remain `?`.
findings.recommendation: Track whether collection is complete and sufficiently supported separately from whether any work was observed. Report zero only when structured information proves a store-hit/no-work request; keep metrics unknown when parsing or metadata correlation is incomplete.

findings.title: Built and cached counts do not advance during an active Nix request
findings.evidence: `consume` processes only `action == "start"` records. It emits `BuildSucceeded` and `SubstituteSucceeded` only from `finish_success`, which `realize_check` calls after `run_logged_command` has returned. Thus, in a request with multiple derivations, a dependency that finishes while other work is still running remains displayed as `to build`/`to fetch`; the `built`/`cached` counts do not reflect that progress until the entire check exits.
findings.recommendation: Consume identity-correlated, success-bearing per-derivation completion evidence as it arrives, and retain unknown status where the protocol cannot establish success.

findings.title: Blocked check completion is delayed until every worker joins
findings.evidence: A failed structure check makes selected traceability `Blocked` at lines 509-517, but this happens after `run_with_followups` has returned; its caller-thread drain waits for the worker tracker to reach zero. The resulting `CheckFinalized` event is sent only in the reconciliation loop at lines 537-547. With a slow Nix task still running, the already-known blocked outcome is omitted from the completion counter until that task finishes.
findings.recommendation: Publish blocked dependent outcomes as soon as their prerequisite failure makes them final, and publish queued `not_run` outcomes when admission is permanently stopped rather than waiting for all active workers.

findings.title: No initial progress snapshot is rendered
findings.evidence: `ProgressReporter::new` stores the initial reducer and line without rendering. `apply` writes only when `reducer.apply(event)` reports a changed snapshot, and `run_checks` starts execution without applying an initialization event. An eligible run therefore emits no `checks 0/N`/unknown-metrics line while its first long-running task has not yet produced a metric event, contrary to the specified initial snapshot behavior.
findings.recommendation: Render the initialized snapshot once after run allocation and before starting workers; continue suppressing subsequent writes unless the displayed tuple changes.

findings.title: Progress width can exceed the actual terminal width and wrap
findings.evidence: `from_environment` records `COLUMNS`, and `width()` trusts that value or defaults to 80 without querying the stderr terminal. For example, with a 60-column terminal and `COLUMNS=80`, the sample snapshot selects the 64-character second format candidate, so it wraps; later `\r\x1b[K` clears only the current row. This violates the no-wrap behavior for narrow terminals.
findings.recommendation: Obtain the width from the stderr terminal using a platform adapter, with a conservative fallback when querying fails, and use that width for formatting and replacement.

findings.title: Piped Nix stderr log-write failures are silently discarded
findings.evidence: When progress is active, the stderr reader ignores errors from `log_for_stderr.write_all` and `flush`, and the caller ignores the reader thread's join result. If retaining stderr fails, the backend can still return the child’s success/failure with a truncated invocation log, despite the plan requiring retained-log I/O failures to be operational errors.
findings.recommendation: Return the reader's first read/write/flush error from the thread and convert retained-log failures to an operational error after reaping the child; keep parser errors best-effort.
